problems.note: Near-duplicate of tap-6 (both are about the sun coming up each day), and both are easy for a skill that is meant to teach ordering repeating events. Consider swapping in a different cycle, such as the moon or a weekly routine, for variety. Keep the answer as is.

output.notes: I checked every card and item against the stated answers. All 15 marked answers are correct, and no distractor is partly right. Each one is a single unambiguous choice. The seasons facts match Ontario: four seasons, winter is cold and snowy, and many trees grow new leaves in spring. The story cards define a cycle accurately and sequence day/night and the seasons correctly. Every item can be understood by ear, since the narration includes the full question and all choices. No content stereotypes anyone or frightens a child. Only the note above is worth raising. Wording such as "the sun comes up" and "the sun goes down" is ordinary Grade 1 language for what children observe, so I did not flag it as a misconception.
